analysis_steps.goal: Run 3D hydrodynamical simulations of binary-disc interaction

method.value: FARGO3D spherical grid, point-mass companion, locally isothermal; cold (h=0.1), hot (h=0.2) and vertically stratified temperature (upper layers 4x midplane, z_q = 3H) runs

evidence.quote: The simulations shown in this paper have been run with the code FARGO3D
with the normalization set such that the disc aspect ratio at the location of the companion is 0.1 for the cold simulation and 0.2 for the hot simulation.
We employ a spherical grid with 250, 80 and 512 cells
The companion is treated like a point mass at a radius $r=1$, with a companion to star ratio $M_2/M_1=0.17$.

key_parameters.value: alpha viscosity 1e-3; images after 90 orbits at 30 au

evidence.quote: a physical viscosity using the (cite: shakurasunyaev) prescription with a value of $\alpha=10^{-3}$
All the images shown are after 90 orbits at a radius of 30 au (roughly 13 orbits at the companion location).
we assume that the temperature in the upper layers is 4 times the value in the midplane
We also assume that $z_q=3H$, where H is the disc scale-height.

referee_caveats_inferred: Pitch-angle fits use a hand-chosen tracing procedure with beam-based errors; sensitivity to tracing choices is not explored
The comparison between models and data is qualitative (visual) with no quantitative fit to the simulations
Gas density is used to set dust density for the sub-mm image, ignoring dust-gas decoupling for mm grains
The inclination depends strongly on the stellar mass prior (30 vs 35 deg)

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly 100-300 GB of raw visibilities for 2 execution blocks at 8.5 km baselines in Band 7 with one FDM window; calibrated measurement set tens of GB (inferred)
reproducibility.score_reason: Data project code and key imaging settings (robust, beam, rms) are given, but clean parameters, tracing procedure and simulation details are missing; hydro/RT parts need substantial inference.
